rationale: Omen uses inferential statistics to terminate hyperdimensional-computing inference early with accuracy guarantees. This is an algorithmic inference optimizer rather than a new compute kernel or kernel-level scheduling/layout change.

BitSpec is a compiler-architecture co-design that speculates on program-variable bitwidths and relies on hardware monitoring and re-execution for correctness. Although it changes bitwidths, it is a general architecture/compiler mechanism rather than a kernel precision format or kernel implementation.
ShadowLoad introduces attack primitives against hardware stride prefetchers and demonstrates security impacts. It is a microarchitectural security attack paper, not a kernel-style optimization.

Skia adds shadow branch decoding and a Shadow Branch Buffer to improve instruction prefetching in processor front-ends. This is hardware prefetch/branch-prediction architecture, not a compute-kernel contribution.

Hierarchical Prefetching combines software analysis of code bundles with lightweight hardware record-and-replay instruction prefetching. The contribution is processor front-end prefetch architecture, not a kernel or kernel-generating compiler.
The paper formally models and verifies the CXL.cache coherence protocol in Isabelle and reports specification fixes. Formal protocol verification is outside the kernel-style optimization construct.

CtXnL provides software/hardware primitives that let transaction systems selectively manage CXL coherence for metadata and records. The open text describes architectural support and OLTP throughput improvements, but the mechanism is memory-coherence support for transaction processing rather than compute kernels.

ByteFS is a kernel-level file system and SSD-firmware co-design for memory-semantic SSDs with byte/block access and coordinated caching. Despite being operating-system kernel code, it is storage-system support rather than a compute-kernel optimization.
M5 profiles and manages CXL-based tiered memory using hot-page and hot-word trackers in the CXL controller. The contribution is page migration and memory management above compute kernels.
Melody is a CXL memory characterization and performance-analysis framework across devices, platforms, and workloads. It reports measurement insights rather than proposing kernel-level optimizations.

MoE-Lightning uses CPU-GPU-I/O pipeline scheduling, paged weights, and a performance model to run MoE batch inference on memory-constrained GPUs. These are offloading and memory-management policies above kernels, so it is not kernel-style under the codebook.

FSMoE abstracts MoE modules and schedules communication, computation, and gradient aggregation for flexible sparse-MoE training. It is a distributed training scheduling system rather than a kernel or compiler/DSL that emits kernels.
